Summary of the el-picker codebase:

---

## File paths

| Purpose | File Path |
|--------|-----------|
| **Selector generation, DOM traversal, element picking** | `/Users/ken/git/vb/el-picker/content.js` |

Selector logic and DOM traversal live in `content.js`; there are no separate modules for selectors or DOM walking.

---

## 1. CSS selector generation

**Function:** `getCssSelector(element)` (lines 54–91)

**Algorithm:**
- Walks up from the target element to `document.body` via `el.parentNode`.
- For each ancestor:
  - If it has an `id`, use `#id` and stop.
  - Otherwise build a selector from:
    - Tag name (lowercase)
    - Up to 2 classes (skipping `elpicker-` prefixed ones)
    - `:nth-of-type(n)` when there are multiple same-tag siblings
- Joins segments with ` > `.

**Relevant code:**

```55:91:/Users/ken/git/vb/el-picker/content.js
  function getCssSelector(element) {
    if (!element) return '';
    if (element.id) return `#${element.id}`;

    const parts = [];
    let el = element;

    while (el && el.nodeType === 1 && el !== document.body) {
      let selector = el.tagName.toLowerCase();

      if (el.id) {
        selector = `#${el.id}`;
        parts.unshift(selector);
        break;
      }

      if (el.className && typeof el.className === 'string') {
        const classes = el.className.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(c => c && !c.startsWith('elpicker-'));
        if (classes.length > 0) {
          selector += '.' + classes.slice(0, 2).join('.');
        }
      }

      const parent = el.parentNode;
      if (parent) {
        const siblings = Array.from(parent.children).filter(c => c.tagName === el.tagName);
        if (siblings.length > 1) {
          const index = siblings.indexOf(el) + 1;
          selector += `:nth-of-type(${index})`;
        }
      }

      parts.unshift(selector);
      el = el.parentNode;
    }

    return parts.join(' > ');
  }
```

---

## 2. DOM tree walking

| Function | Lines | Role |
|----------|-------|------|
| `getCssSelector` | 61–88 | Walks up via `el.parentNode` |
| `getXPath` | 34–52 | Walks up recursively via `getXPath(element.parentNode)` |
| `getBreadcrumb` | 94–118 | Walks up via `el.parentElement` (max 5 levels) |
| `navigateParent` | 514–520 | Uses `parentElement` |
| `navigateChild` | 522–432 | Uses `children` |
| `navigateSiblingPrev` / `navigateSiblingNext` | 534–558 | Use `parent.children` and index |
| `getElementsInRect` | 354–371 | Uses `document.elementsFromPoint` |
| `findBestMatchInRect` | 373–398 | Uses `document.elementsFromPoint` |
| `onMouseMove` / `onMouseUp` | 443–501 | Use `document.elementFromPoint` for click/drag |

---

## 3. Selector preference / avoidance

**Preferences:**
- Prefer `id`: if present, use `#id` and stop (shortest path).
- Prefer classes: up to 2 classes per node.
- Use `:nth-of-type` only when needed (multiple same-tag siblings).

**Avoidance:**
- Ignore classes starting with `elpicker-` (lines 71, 103).
- No explicit handling for dynamic classes, data attributes, or `role`.

**Not implemented:**
- Uniqueness checks (e.g. `querySelector` to verify one match).
- Preference for `data-*` or `role` over classes.
- Avoidance of `:nth-of-type` when other attributes suffice.
- Shortest-path optimization (e.g. stopping when selector is unique).

---

## 4. Output format dispatch

**Function:** `getElementContext(element)` (lines 120–133)

Dispatches to `getXPath`, `getCssSelector`, or raw HTML based on `state.outputFormat` (`'xpath'`, `'selector'`, `'outerhtml'`, `'innerhtml'`). Default is `'selector'` (line 25).
